evidence_updates.update: Eureka's primary report explicitly states 50,000 repeated-search tasks: independent re-exploration succeeds 58.488% versus 24.492% when the first open-search output is forcibly reused; 30,000 adversarial surface-similar artifact pairs yield 100% false merge for approximate semantic merging versus 0% for exact/certified merge; deterministic runtime optimizations alter open-action ordering in 0/12,000 frontiers. Reproducibility boundary: the current public repository tree, checked-in tests, SHA256 manifest, and releases expose the paper-aligned runtime implementation but no obvious benchmark-generation scripts, raw result files, seeds, or manifests for these 50k/30k suites; releases are empty. Preserve these numbers as primary-paper claims rather than independently reproduced results until a supporting artifact is found.

The same Eureka public-artifact audit applies to governed-evolution and architecture-promotion quantitative ablations: the implementation exposes evolution/runtime control code, but the checked public tree does not obviously contain the full experiment harness/raw outputs needed to independently reproduce the reported policy table. Keep the within-paper matched-policy result as useful primary evidence with an explicit reproducibility limitation.

AutoResearchClaw's T10 case study further sharpens the verification boundary: 51 logged metric keys can be numerically genuine yet scientifically non-discriminative when all conditions collapse to identical zero values. A measurement-bound registry blocks invented numbers but must be paired with a separate evidence-adequacy/discrimination check.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Diversity-first bounded epistemic deliberation with marginal-information gating
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: In AutoResearchClaw's scientific pipeline, removing structured Debate from the same 10-topic best-of-3 component ablation lowers selected-output quality from 5.62 to 4.25 (delta -1.37, reported p=0.003) while the debate panel uses complementary roles. Its design-space study tests K in {2,3,5} over 10 runs each: K=2 reduces hypothesis diversity by 23%; K=5 costs 67% more tokens for only 8% more diversity than K=3. Independent controlled debate work supports the boundary: diversity-aware initialization raises Pass@5 from 0.7921 to 0.9097 for Qwen2.5-7B and from 0.7423 to 0.9026 for Llama-3.1-8B, while a separate N=10 homogeneous-debate study finds modal adoption up to 85.5%, correct-reasoning vulnerability up to 70.0%, oracle gaps up to 32.3 points, and 2.1-3.4x token use for equal/lower accuracy than isolated self-correction.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Use a small panel only when it adds genuinely different epistemic views; optimize initial hypothesis diversity and complementary roles before adding rounds/agents. More communication or more homogeneous agents is not a monotonic capability scaler. Deliberation should expand only when expected marginal diversity/information exceeds token and conformity cost.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Direct scientific-agent causal evidence for Debate is small (10 ML research topics, best-of-3) and K=3 is a tuned point, not a universal constant. The independent confidence/diversity and homogeneous-debate studies use reasoning QA rather than open scientific discovery, so they constrain mechanism design rather than proving transfer.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Evidence-structured hypothesis-tree memory with distilled insight propagation
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: Arbor ablates its persistent hypothesis tree and upward distilled-insight feedback on MLE-Bench Lite with the same tool access, workspace budget, evaluation protocol, and Claude Opus 4.6 backbone. All variants retain 100% valid submissions, but Full Arbor reaches 81.82% Any Medal versus 63.64% without the tree and 54.54% without insight feedback. The tree binds hypotheses, artifact versions, evidence, and compact causal insights; executors are isolated and cannot mutate shared state, while the coordinator receives only structured results and ancestor insights.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Long-horizon research memory should preserve the branching hypothesis/evidence structure and propagate compact reusable causal lessons, rather than treating chronological transcripts or a flat experiment queue as the main research state. The larger drop from disabling insight feedback than flattening the tree suggests semantic lesson propagation is a first-order component, not merely bookkeeping.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: Matched autonomous-research ablation on MLE-Bench Lite, not a full decomposition of every Arbor component. The evaluation is autonomous optimization of research artifacts with programmatic/held-out evaluators, so transfer to wet-lab or theory discovery remains unproven.

candidate_mechanisms_new.mechanism: Selective forgetting / utility-gated retention for cross-run research lessons
candidate_mechanisms_new.evidence: AutoResearchClaw's lesson store weights lessons by severity and exponential time decay. Its 10-run design-space sensitivity tests half-lives {7,15,30,60,infinity}: 7 days expires useful lessons too quickly, infinity accumulates contradictory advice after 15 runs, and 30 days gives the best reported quality trajectory while affecting roughly 3-5 later runs. Independently, a controlled LLM-agent memory study finds error propagation and misaligned experience replay under naive accumulation; combining selective addition and deletion yields about 10 percentage points average absolute performance gain versus naive memory growth.
candidate_mechanisms_new.interpretation: Persistent research experience should not be append-only. Retention should depend on current utility, evidence quality, recency and contradiction risk, with explicit deletion/decay of stale or harmful lessons. Fixed temporal decay is one implementation; the stronger transferable principle is quality/utility-gated survival.
candidate_mechanisms_new.scope: AutoResearchClaw's 30-day optimum is system- and cadence-specific and reported qualitatively, not a universal half-life. The selective-add/delete gain is from general LLM-agent tasks rather than autonomous science. A matched scientific-agent comparison of fixed time decay versus utility/evidence-gated forgetting is still needed.

negative_and_boundary_evidence_new: Structured debate should not be generalized to 'more agents/rounds improve science'. A controlled N=10 homogeneous-agent study reports strong conformity and fragility at low communication density, plus 2.1-3.4x token cost for equal or lower accuracy than isolated self-correction.

A preregistered within-paper study of AI feedback on 44 economics meta-analyses found authors preferred a single frontier-model pass to two multi-agent debate systems by 0.66 and 0.57 mean rank points, while the larger workshop used about 30x tokens. Three AI judges also almost always ranked the real human referee report last, whereas authors who remembered it usually ranked it first and never last. This is direct evidence against using multi-agent complexity or LLM-as-judge agreement as a default proxy for intended-user usefulness.

The paper-feedback study measures perceived usefulness for finished economics meta-analyses, not realized scientific correctness or autonomous experiment quality. It constrains evaluation design and default complexity, not all multi-agent research.

Arbor's ablation makes a flat-vs-tree distinction and an insight-feedback distinction, but it does not isolate every memory operation. Do not attribute the entire gain to any single tree data structure primitive.
AutoResearchClaw's K=3 and 30-day half-life are local design-space optima under its tested ML run cadence. Treat them as evidence for bounded diversity and forgetting, not universal hyperparameters.

Eureka's public code increases inspectability but does not currently make the large repeated-search/adversarial-merge benchmark results obviously reproducible from checked-in harnesses; primary-paper result and independently reproduced evidence remain separate.
